This appendix summarizes OPALX input syntax. Italic names denote syntactic
entities, while monospaced tokens must be entered literally. Attribute-specific
restrictions belong to the corresponding command reference.

## Statements

| Entity | Form |
|---|---|
| _comment_ | `// ...` or `/* ... */` |
| _identifier_ | `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*` |
| _integer_ | `[0-9]+` |
| _string_ | single-quoted or double-quoted text |
| _command_ | `_keyword_;` or `_keyword_, _attribute-list_;`, optionally preceded by `_label_ :` |
| _attribute-list_ | One attribute followed by zero or more `, _attribute_` entries. |
| _attribute_ | `_attribute-name_`, `_attribute-name_ = _attribute-value_`, or `_attribute-name_ := _attribute-value_` |

Unquoted identifiers and keywords are case-insensitive: the lexer normalizes
them to upper case. Quoted text preserves its case. A hyphen is not part of an
unquoted identifier.

For real and logical expression-valued attributes, `=` evaluates immediately,
whereas `:=` retains an expression for later evaluation. This distinction is
not universal: string values are parsed and stored immediately with either
operator. Use `=` for real constant definitions; `:=` is not supported there.

Structured statements and macro definitions/calls have additional forms; see
[Control Statements](../../control-statements/index.qmd).

The accepted value category depends on the attribute's registered type.
Categories used by supported input interfaces include:

- string expression
- logical expression
- real expression
- array expression
- variable reference
- place
- range
- token list
- token-list array
- regular expression

## Real Expressions

| Entity | Form |
|---|---|
| _real-expression_ | `_real-term_`, unary `+/- _real-term_`, or recursive `+` / `-` combinations |
| _real-term_ | `_real-factor_` or recursive `*` / `/` combinations |
| _real-factor_ | `_real-primary_` or `_real-primary_ ^ _real-primary_` |
| _real-primary_ | real literal, symbolic constant, `#` inside a `TABLE` generator, real name, array lookup, object attribute lookup, table reference, function call, or parenthesized expression |

A factor accepts at most one exponentiation operator. Write `(a^b)^c` or
`a^(b^c)` when grouping powers; an unparenthesized `a^b^c` is not accepted.

Built-in scalar functions include:

- `RANF`, `GAUSS`
- `ABS`, `TRUNC`, `ROUND`, `FLOOR`, `CEIL`, `SIGN`
- `SQRT`, `LOG`, `EXP`
- `SIN`, `COS`, `TAN`, `ASIN`, `ACOS`, `ATAN`, `ATAN2`
- `MAX`, `MIN`, `MOD`, `POW`

Functions of arrays are:

- `VMIN`
- `VMAX`
- `VRMS`
- `VABSMAX`

The grammar also allows:

- `_array_[ _index_ ]`
- `_object-name_ -> _real-attribute_`
- `_object-name_ -> _array-attribute_[ _index_ ]`
- `_table-reference_`

## Real Variables and Constants

| Entity | Form |
|---|---|
| _real-prefix_ | `REAL` for variables; `CONST`, `CONSTANT`, `REAL CONST`, or `REAL CONSTANT` for constants. |
| _real-definition_ | `_real-prefix_ _real-name_ = _real-expression_;`. Variables also permit `:=`; real constants use `=`. |
| _symbolic-constant_ | `PI`, `TWOPI`, `DEGRAD`, `RADDEG`, `E`, `EMASS`, `PMASS`, `HMMASS`, `UMASS`, `CMASS`, `MUMASS`, `DMASS`, `XEMASS`, `CLIGHT`, `H2PMASS`, `ALPHAMASS`, `AMU`, `OPALVERSION`, `RANK` |

An existing real variable can be reassigned without repeating its type prefix.
A new bare-name assignment does not declare a variable; use `REAL` when
introducing one.

Unquoted real names, object names, table names, and column names follow
the identifier syntax defined above.

## Logical Expressions and Variables

Logical expressions combine relations using `&&` and `||`. Relations bind
first, then `&&`, then `||`; parentheses group logical expressions. Both
operands are evaluated, so C-style short-circuit behavior must not be assumed.

The relation grammar allows:

- `_logical-name_`
- `( _logical-expression_ )`
- `TRUE`
- `FALSE`
- `_real-expression_ _relation-operator_ _real-expression_`

The relation operators are:

- `==`
- `!=`
- `<`
- `>`
- `>=`
- `<=`

Logical variables use the prefixes:

- `BOOL`
- `BOOL CONST`

and the same `=` versus `:=` distinction as for reals.

## String Expressions and Constants

String expressions may be:

- a literal string
- an existing string-valued name or a known object name; arbitrary unquoted
  text is not a general string literal
- a concatenation `_string-expression_ & _string_`

String definitions use the prefix `STRING`:

- `STRING name = expression`
- `STRING name := expression`

String parsing stores the value immediately for both forms; `:=` does not
create a deferred string expression.

## Real Array Expressions and Definitions

Array expressions support the following arithmetic operations:

- unary `+` and `-`
- binary `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`
- exponentiation
- parentheses

The array primaries are:

- `{ _array-literal_ }`
- `_array-reference_`
- `_real-function_( _array-expression_ )`
- `( _array-expression_ )`

The array literal grammar is recursive:

- `_array-literal_ : _real-expression_`
- `_array-literal_ : _array-literal_ , _real-expression_`

Array references may be:

- `_array-name_`
- `_object-name_ -> _array-attribute_`

Real array definitions use:

- `_array-prefix_ : VECTOR` or `REAL VECTOR`
- `_array-definition_ : _array-prefix_ _array-name_ = _array-expression_`
- `_array-definition_ : _array-prefix_ _array-name_ := _array-expression_`

`VECTOR` and `REAL VECTOR` declare a global real array; `ARRAY` is not a
declaration keyword. Braces form array values, including array-valued command
attributes. For example:

```opal
REAL VECTOR V = {1, 2, 3};
VECTOR W := {1, 2, 3};
```

The exponentiation grouping rule above also applies to real arrays.

## Variable References

A variable reference names a real variable or an object attribute:

- `_variable-reference_ : _real-name_`
- `_variable-reference_ : _object-name_ -> _attribute-name_`

This is the basic hook that lets later statements reuse parser-visible values
and object attributes.

## Token Lists and Regular Expressions

The final grammar sections define parser tokens that are not scalar numbers.

Token lists:

- A token list ends at a top-level comma, semicolon or closing delimiter.
  Balanced nested `()`, `[]` and `{}` remain part of the list.
- `_token-list-array_ : _token-list_`
- `_token-list-array_ : { _token-list_, ... }` for multiple token lists

Regular expressions:

- `_regular-expression_ : "` _UNIX-regular-expression_ `"`

These forms appear mostly in higher-level command attributes and parser-side
matching constructs rather than in beam-dynamics expressions.
